### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, touching **24** documentable anchor(s).

**33** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 369bcbeda7bb6c2cbc8c3c3892435351506c960c`.

⛔ **8** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `os validate (command, 51 pages)`
- **8** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **207** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **153** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **153**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **98** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **25** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 369bcbeda7bb6c2cbc8c3c3892435351506c960c` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `6354c6fd4225f6329ea5537328fd292ad9ba4554` — the merge of head `0fb378cfdb022b1fbdcc19ed91df3c359c2b852a` into base `369bcbeda7bb6c2cbc8c3c3892435351506c960c`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 6354c6fd4225f6329ea5537328fd292ad9ba4554 && git checkout 6354c6fd4225f6329ea5537328fd292ad9ba4554
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 369bcbeda7bb6c2cbc8c3c3892435351506c960c 0fb378cfdb022b1fbdcc19ed91df3c359c2b852a && git checkout -B drift-repro 369bcbeda7bb6c2cbc8c3c3892435351506c960c && git merge --no-ff 0fb378cfdb022b1fbdcc19ed91df3c359c2b852a

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 369bcbeda7bb6c2cbc8c3c3892435351506c960c
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 369bcbeda7bb6c2cbc8c3c3892435351506c960c` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `08a046af36360d77aa3a0e24e38cf75217ce11c3`

### ① Derived judgments
- "No top-level key is added" to any `--json` output — validate/build spread `jsxGateNotices` into the existing `warningsSoFar()` (head `packages/cli/src/commands/validate.ts` lines 183–192, success payload line 720, catch-all line 828; `compile.ts` lines 45–53, payload line 997 and catch-all); lint pushes `jsxGate.notices.map(authoringFindingToLintIssue)` into `issues` (`lint.ts` lines 970–972). Pin "the payloads grow no new top-level key" compares key sets with and without the notice. Correct.
- "`--strict` does not promote it on any command" — validate's strict gate reads the local `warnings: string[]` built at `validate.ts` lines 668–700 (exit set at line 772 and line 801), which never receives `jsxGateNotices`; lint's `failing = errors + (strict ? warnings : 0)` (`lint.ts` lines 1013–1017) and the notice is graded `suggestion`; build has no `--strict`. Pins: `noManifest` under `--strict` exits 0 on validate and lint. Correct.
- Existing channel, existing severity — `AuthoringSeverity = 'error' | 'warning' | 'info'` (`packages/lint/src/authoring-rules.ts` line 178); `ruleAdvisories` already carries `AuthoringFinding` records in the payload's `warnings` (`validate.ts` line 140) and `validate-approval-approvers.ts` / `validate-security-posture.ts` already emit `info`; lint's `suggestion` is the pre-existing `info` to `suggestion` mapping (`lint.ts` line 765). Correct.
- Exit codes unchanged in the missing-manifest case — the `absent` branch of `resolveJsxGateManifest` (`packages/cli/src/utils/sdui-manifest.ts` lines 214–258) returns notices only, never throws; pins exit 0 on all three text and json faces. Correct.
- Refusal fires only when there is a kind:'html' page to check — `if (pages === 0) return` at line 220 precedes the `unusable` branch at line 222; pin `noPagesMalformed` exits 0 with empty stderr. Correct as a one-direction statement. The converse the changeset asserts ("kind:'html' pages present: a notice" / "refused when the project has a kind:'html' page to check") is WRONG on one layout — see ③, union-fold gap.
- No ADR-0112 code minted — `SduiManifestRefusalError` (lines 184–196) carries only `reportedToStderr` and `hints`; `errorCodeFields` reads exactly `code` and `httpStatus` (`format.ts` lines 278–286); unit pin asserts `errorCodeFields(e)` equals `{}`. Correct.
- Kind set parity — `validateJsxPages` (`packages/lint/src/validate-jsx-pages.ts` lines 43–58) checks `kind === 'html' || 'jsx'` over `collectionEntries(stack.pages)` and refuses empty or non-string `source` before any manifest read; `countJsxGatePages` (lines 162–175) uses the same two kinds, the same array/map handling with non-record skip as `collection-entries.ts`, and excludes empty source. `'jsx'` is a deprecated alias (`page.zod.ts` lines 839–843). The driven parity over eight kinds with a non-vacuity check holds. Correct.
- `os build` exits 1, not 2 — compile.ts catch-all takes `this.exit(1)` on `isReportedError` before `this.error()`. Correct.
- Before-table (invalid JSON / `null` / unreadable silent at exit 0; `{}` / array crash at exit 1) — base `resolveSduiManifest`: `if (parsed) return parsed` lets `null` fall through, `catch {}` swallows read and JSON errors; `authoring-rules.ts` line 1040 hands the manifest to the rule when truthy, so `{}` reaches `compile()`'s `Object.keys(manifest.components)`. Correct.
- "`os init`'s scaffold check reads the manifest as it did" — `scaffold-validate.ts` lines 93–97 map `resolved` to the manifest, else `undefined`; a wrong-shape file previously reached the rule as a truthy object. No scaffold under `packages/cli/src` declares a `kind: 'html'` or `'jsx'` page (grep), so the manifest is never dereferenced on that door and the reading is observationally unchanged. Correct with that caveat.
- "then the copy inside `@objectstack/console`" — `packages/console/package.json` `exports` publishes only `./package.json`, so the specifier cannot resolve on any install (#19922). The changeset says only that it is looked for, and the notice names it. Not false; the hint names a dead location until #19922 lands.
- Published docs — `sdui.manifest` appears nowhere in `content/docs/**` or `skills/**`; `deployment/cli.mdx` lines 667–675 list the `--strict` warning set (the notice is not gated, so still true); `cli.mdx` lines 1551–1560 say suggestions stay advisory (true); `validating-metadata.mdx` line 435 "JSX / React page source parses" stays true; no `os validate --json` `warnings` shape is documented anywhere. No page becomes false and none needed to change. Correct.
- Changeset wording nit — "Each command prints one line": `printJsxGateNotices` (lines 260–265) prints the info line plus a dim hint line; lint prints via `printIssue`. One record, two lines. Not a claim of substance.

### ② Semver level
- Ruling: `Clause-②: no` with `patch` is right. By the repo's own reader (`scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs` lines 69–95) `no (narrowing)` is for a diff that narrows a PUBLISHED accept set. The narrowed population — a present `sdui.manifest.json` that is invalid JSON, `null`, unreadable, or without a `components` map — was never a member of a published set: the file is named in no `content/docs` or `skills` page; ADR-0080 §3–§4 define the manifest as the serialized registry carrying `components`, and its status line records manifest validation as not wired; half the class (`{}`, array, string) already exited 1 via a bare TypeError, so no coherent accept set existed to narrow; and the exit 0 was a `catch {}` fall-through, exactly what AGENTS.md rule 3 orders removed ("prefer failing to falling back"). Precedent: `.changeset/15293-non-array-packages-refusal.md` (`@objectstack/runtime: patch`, `Clause-②: no`) refused a schema-malformed value on the same terms. Contrast: the ADR-0080 `type=` refusal (`packages/sdui-parser/CHANGELOG.md`, "This narrows what the html tier accepts") narrowed the documented page-`source` grammar and was ruled a narrowing by the maintainer; this PR narrows no documented grammar. The changeset carries the consumer fix line ("correct the file, or remove it"). No BREAKING banner and no ADR-0087 marker are owed.

### ③ Boundary flags
- Refuse vs notice for an unusable project manifest — Answer: refuse (option A), as shipped. AGENTS.md rule 3; the author placed the file and the remedy is named; option B keeps a green over a file the author wrote (the card's defect one layer down); option C refuses a file nothing reads. Reach is bounded: 0 in-tree examples carry the file and no doc names it.
- `scaffold-validate.ts` edited outside the claimed surface — Answer: acceptable; mechanically forced by the resolver's return type, behaviour preserved (resolved to manifest, else `undefined`), and unobservable on `os init` since no scaffold ships an html page. Declared in the PR body; no change required.
- New pin file in the integration tier (~53 s, 18 spawns) — Answer: rename it `jsx-gate-manifest-notice.e2e.test.ts`. Every sibling pin that spawns `bin/run-dev.js` is `.e2e` (`build-json-failure-conversions.e2e.test.ts`, `lint-conversion-notices.e2e.test.ts`, `validate-json-failure-conversions.e2e.test.ts`), and the maintainer direction recorded in `packages/cli/vitest.config.ts` lines 596–611 moved that class out of the per-PR and queue runs by name; the logic is already held by the unit file. If the seat wants the exit-code pins in the queue, keep only the `malformed` and `noPagesMalformed` spawns there.
- FOUND, union-fold gap (the required change) — `resolveJsxGateManifest` counts pages over `authoringRuleUnionStack(...)` alone, and that fold returns the stack BY IDENTITY whenever the top level carries any `pages` key, `[]` included (`packages/cli/src/utils/stack-collections.ts` line 362). The per-package pass then judges each `packages[].manifest` body as its own stack with the same `sduiManifest` (`packages/cli/src/utils/artifact-packages.ts` lines 300–304), and `AssembledPackageBodySchema` admits `pages` there (`packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts` line 1017 `pages: 'concat'`; `ArtifactPackageSchema` lines 1482–1490). So a stack with a top-level `pages` key (`[]`, or a `kind: 'full'` page) plus html pages inside `packages[]`: count is 0, no notice, and the per-package pass parse-checks those pages in silence — the card's defect; with an `unusable` manifest the early return at `sdui-manifest.ts` line 220 bypasses the refusal and the run exits 0. Both changeset bullets state the opposite for that layout. Same on all three commands (`lintConfig` runs the same per-package pass with `opts.sduiManifest`).
- CI at head — 32 check runs: 20 success, 3 skipped, 9 in progress (Test Core 1–6, Temporal Conformance, Lint & Repo Gates, Type Check · workspace), 0 failure at read time. Not green yet.
- Minor — the `absent` notice always names the console specifier, which cannot resolve on any install while `@objectstack/console` exports only `./package.json`; harmless, sends a reader to a dead location until #19922. Noted, not required.
- Minor — the pin's `noticesIn` reads `warnings` first and `issues` only when `warnings` is absent; a command carrying both would be half-read. Not reachable today.

Reviewed-by: `session_01UYBdGBzWSrAMzpW8ah3GbP`

**VERDICT: FAIL**
- Count the JSX-gate pages over every stack the gate judges — the union fold PLUS each `packages[].manifest` body the per-package pass hands `validateJsxPages` (de-duplicated when the fold already folded `pages`) — so the notice and the `unusable` refusal fire whenever any html/jsx page will be parse-checked; carry the corrected count in the notice message; add a pin with a top-level `pages` key (`[]` and a `kind: 'full'` page) beside package-carried html pages that asserts the notice on all three commands and exit 1 with a malformed manifest; then re-read the two changeset bullets against it.

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `0fb378cfdb022b1fbdcc19ed91df3c359c2b852a`

Delta of: `5852657026` (FAIL on `08a046af`)

### ① Derived judgments
- Required change, enumeration — `jsxGateStacks` (`packages/cli/src/utils/sdui-manifest.ts` lines 169–174) returns `[authoringRuleUnionStack(stack), ...artifactPackages(stack).map(pkg => packageBodyAsStack(pkg.body, stack.packages))]`, which is byte-for-byte the pass's own walk in `runPerPackageAuthoringRules` (`artifact-packages.ts` lines 291–300: `artifactPackages(run.parsed)` then `packageBodyAsStack(pkg.body, run.parsed.packages)`); no second walk of `packages[]`. Option B: the fold spreads the same page objects with the same names (`collectFrom`), one key each; additive: the top-level union carries the bodies' names, one key each; both pinned (unit lines 195–207, expecting 3 and 2). Map-shaped pages: the fold's record branch (`stack-collections.ts` lines 372–378) preserves map keys and `collectionEntries` injects the map key as `name`, so the count keys and the gate's `page "NAME"` agree. Unnamed array pages are unreachable through a parsed stack (`PageSchema.name` is `SnakeCaseIdentifierSchema`, required, `page.zod.ts` line 764; `stack.zod.ts` line 379 is `z.array(PageSchema)`); on lint's unparsed input they fall to record identity, which the fold preserves. Under-count on a name collision, not a silent degradation; noted, not required.
- New unit pins fail without the round-1 fix — with the per-package leg removed the fold alone reds exactly: the two PACKAGE_CARRIED count pins (0 not 1), the `jsxGateStacks` equality pin, the option-B length-3 pin, the two absent-notice pins and the two unusable-refusal pins = 8, while additive and already-folded stay green; 35 tests in the file (8+11+6+9+1).
